subject: PO entity split, invoice failover mechanics & EU VAT evidence
messages:
From: Procurement - Nimbus Health <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order Form billing split & PO (Nimbus Health)

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nimbus is ready to move the pilot to a paid order. A couple of procurement asks before we sign the Order Form:

- We need invoicing split between Nimbus US, Inc. (for US-hosted workloads) and Nimbus Health UK Ltd (for EMEA usage). Can Redwood accept multiple invoice recipients on the same Order Form (we prefer separate invoices per legal entity)?
- Net payment terms: procurement will try for Net 30; legal may push for Net 45. Please confirm what Redwood can accept and whether an early-pay discount is available.
- Tax residency / reverse-charge: for the UK/EU entity we need evidence that Redwood can support reverse-charge (we will need a VAT invoice and a form).
- Attached is the initial PO (Nimbus_PO_45321.pdf).

We also saw references to a "billing fallback" in the MSA — can you confirm how Redwood handles billing if the billed entity changes mid-term (e.g., entity migration or acquisition)? We need a clear path so our accounting team can map GL codes.

Appreciate a short call to confirm.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health
procurement@nimbushealth.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form billing split & PO (Nimbus Health)

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list and for the PO. Quick answers and next steps below.

Summary answers:
- Split invoices: yes — we can issue separate invoices to two legal entities on the same commercial agreement provided each billed entity is named on the Order Form and has separate billing contacts/PO numbers.
- Terms: Redwood typically supports Net 30 on hosted orders; Net 45 is possible for enterprise with an approved finance exception. We can offer a 1.5% early-pay discount for payment within 10 days if that helps.
- Tax / reverse-charge: we can accommodate EU reverse-charge flows, but we will need the customer's VAT ID and the signed evidence per our tax checklist.
- Billing fallback / failover: proposed language (we will send a draft redline) that allows Redwood to route invoices to a designated holding entity if the named billed entity cannot receive invoices; any subsequent inter-entity reconciliation is managed via a credit note between the parties (this is important for accounting).

Attached: draft_orderform_redline.docx — includes: billing entity table, PO field per entity, net terms options, and the billing failover clause.

Can you confirm (a) the two exact legal entity names and billing addresses, (b) whether procurement prefers separate POs per entity (we can accept one PO that lists both entities, but finance prefers separate PO numbers), and (c) Nimbus's VAT IDs for the UK/EMEA entity(s)? Once we have that, I'll loop in Kimberly in finance and Ben on the commercial side; legal redlines can be coordinated after your internal review.

If you'd like a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk the redline, I'm available 10:00–12:00 PT.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com
+1 (650) 555-0199

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Order Form billing split & PO (Nimbus Health) — need legal/finance review

Ben / Kim / Lauren — forwarding Nimbus procurement's ask and the draft redline I just sent. High level asks from Nimbus: separate entity invoices, net terms flexibility, and EU reverse-charge evidence.

Action items (please):
- Ben: confirm commercial stance on minimum commit allocation if customer asks to split the commit across legal entities. Do we accept splitting the minimum commit, or do we require the commit to be allocated to a single billed entity?
- Kimberly: confirm finance requirements for issuing separate invoices (fields you need on the Order Form), and whether the billing failover clause below is acceptable operationally.
- Lauren (legal): quick read of the proposed billing failover wording in the draft — we want a clean mechanism to: (1) invoice a fallback entity if the named billed entity becomes non-responsive, and (2) allow Redwood to raise credit notes to correct inter-entity allocations later.

Proposed billing-failover clause (excerpt from the draft):
"If the billed entity named on the Order Form is unable to accept invoices (e.g., entity dissolution, acquisition, or administrative hold), Customer shall designate an alternate billing entity within ten (10) business days. If no designation is provided, Redwood may issue invoices to the Customer's parent or holding entity as identified in the MSA. Redwood will issue corrective credit notes or debit notes to reflect the final inter-entity allocation once the parties confirm the correct billed entity."

Please review and post comments in the draft redline (I've attached). We are targeting signature this week — would like to firm the ask back to the customer by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Priya

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form billing split & PO (Nimbus Health) — need legal/finance review

Priya / Kim — quick commercial take:

- We do not generally split the minimum committed spend across multiple legal entities in a way that reduces Redwood's forecastable revenue. If Nimbus insists on compartmentalizing usage by entity we can accept separate invoices, but the minimum commit must either be: (a) apportioned by clear % on the Order Form with acceptance from both entities, or (b) assigned to a single master billed entity.
- Credit note process for inter-entity reconciliation is fine as long as finance confirms the process is simple (one credit note per billing period ideally).

For urgency: if Nimbus sends separate POs per entity today, I propose we accept them but add an explicit sentence: "Minimum commit allocation will be governed by section X of the Order Form and is not released until both entities have signed." That will avoid ambiguity.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercials
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form billing split & PO (Nimbus Health) — finance checklist

Thanks for the context. Finance read:

- Separate invoices per legal entity: operationally fine. Required fields per invoice: billed entity name, billing address, PO number, tax ID / VAT ID, billing contact email, and a line for the Redwood order number.
- Billing failover: acceptable if we keep the corrective credit note window limited to 90 days after initial invoice issuance (longer windows create revenue recognition issues).
- Minimum commit: prefer allocation to a single entity for revenue predictability. If the customer insists on apportionment, require: (1) explicit allocation table in the Order Form, (2) a primary billed entity responsible for any uncollected shortfall, and (3) both entity POs to reference the master deal id (Deal NIM-2026-11-21-02).
- Tax evidence: we need a completed tax-evidence-checklist.pdf and customer VAT ID. For reverse-charge, request: VAT registration number + statement of intra-EU supply.

I'll attach the checklist and a sample Order Form billing table we prefer. Attaching tax-evidence-checklist.pdf.

Kimberly Park
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

- Entities & POs: Nimbus US, Inc. (PO #US-45321) and Nimbus Health UK Ltd (PO #UK-45321). Attached is the signed PO bundle (Nimbus_PO_45321.pdf). We will have our legal team review the redline but procurement is fine with the billing-failover wording subject to legal comment.
- Minimum commit: procurement prefers the commit to be apportioned by percentage across the two entities. We accept the primary billed-entity fallback approach proposed if Redwood requires a single primary for revenue recognition.
- VAT: UK entity VAT ID: GB123456789. We will provide the reverse-charge statement and completed tax-evidence-checklist by tomorrow.

Please incorporate: (1) a billing table in the Order Form that lists each entity, billing address, PO number and VAT ID, (2) explicit language about credit notes for inter-entity adjustments (we are ok with a 90-day correction window), and (3) a reference in the Order Form to the MSA section that authorizes Redwood to invoice a parent/holding entity in a failover scenario.

If you can send an updated redline today we'll aim to route to legal and sign by EOD Monday.

Best,
Alice Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health
